# Documentation requirements for site packages

This part of the site packages help is for anyone who builds, changes or reviews a site installer package: a
developer forking `sevenx_multisite`, a designer shipping a starter site, a partner preparing a package for a
customer, or a reviewer of a pull request to the package server. It answers one question: **what must a package
carry, and what should it carry, before it is published?**

Every requirement here was taken from the code that reads a package (`kernel/classes/ezpackage.php`,
`kernel/classes/ezpackageuploadinspector.php`, `kernel/classes/exppackagejson.php`, the setup wizard steps in
`kernel/setup/steps/`) and from the 16 packages in the two 7x source repositories,
[se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage) (14 packages) and
[se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage) (2 packages).

## Two kinds of requirement

Each page marks every item with one of two labels:

| Label | Meaning | What happens when it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| **Enforced** | The code refuses the package, skips it, or stops the install | The import fails, the wizard does not list the package, or the install ends with an error |
| **Convention** | Every shipped 7x package does it, and the pages and tools that show a package rely on it | The package works, but a reader, a reviewer or a later release has less to go on |

A pull request to the package server is reviewed against both. "It imports" is the lowest bar, not the goal:
see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## The checklist in short

The full list with the reason for each item is [The requirements checklist](the-requirements-checklist.md).

- [ ] **Enforced**: the archive is a gzip compressed tar with `package.xml` at its top, only plain files and
      directories, no `..` and no absolute paths.
- [ ] **Enforced**: `<name>` is lower case letters, digits and `_` only. **Convention**: the `.ezpkg` file carries
      the same name.
- [ ] **Enforced** (package upload in the administration): `<ezpublish>` and `<packaging>` are present.
- [ ] **Enforced**: `<version><number>`, `<release>` and `<type value>` are plain tokens of at most 64 characters.
- [ ] **Enforced** (setup wizard): a site package has `<type value="site" />`, and every package it requires is
      listed in the same `index.xml` with a `url`.
- [ ] **Convention**: `<vendor>`, `<summary>`, `<description>`, `<licence>`, `<state>`, a `LICENCE` document,
      one changelog entry per release, a thumbnail in the `default` file collection.
- [ ] **Convention**: the package validates (`Validate` on its page, or `php ezpm.php validate`) before it is
      published.
- [ ] **Convention**: the source repository explains the package in a README and states its license.

## Where the requirements are checked

A package meets the code at four points, and each checks a different set:

| Where | Code | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| Every import (setup wizard download, `ezpm.php import`, administration upload) | `eZPackage::importUnaudited()` | Archive entries, a readable definition with a name, valid name, safe vendor directory, not already present |
| Package upload in the administration (`package/upload`) | `eZPackageUploadInspector::inspect()`, then `expPackageJson::validateDirectory()` | Additionally: file suffix, gzip signature, size limits, `<package>` root, no DOCTYPE, `<ezpublish>` and `<packaging>`, every document well formed |
| The setup wizard's site type step | `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php` | Type `site`, the index entry, every required package downloadable and new enough |
| The create sites step | `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php` | Every required package can be fetched and installed (errors `EZSW-050`, `EZSW-051`) |

> **Note**
> The setup wizard's own download and upload paths call `eZPackage::import()` directly, without the upload
> inspector's definition checks. A package that imports through the wizard can still be refused by the
> administration's upload page. Test both, as [Validating a package before publishing](validating-a-package-before-publishing.md)
> describes.
